citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N)$, $u$, $\nabla$, and the fixed-composition state be as in
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], with
$g(u,u)=-1$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Define
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$\Delta_a{}^b=\delta_a{}^b+u_au^b$, and $D=u^a\nabla_a$,
$\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and the spatial symmetric
trace-free shear

$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)} -\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$

where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Suppose smooth fields
$\Pi$, $Q^a$, $V^a$, and $\pi^{ab}$ obey $u_aQ^a=u_aV^a=0$,
$u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $\pi^{ab}$ is symmetric with $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Set

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab} +u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a+V^a.$$

If $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$, the vector field

$$S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T}$$

satisfies the exact identity

$$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} -\frac{Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)}{T^2} -V^a\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\mu}{T}\right)-\frac{u_bf^b}{T}.$$

This identity applies to the stated smooth fields and conventions; it does not
select a constitutive law or assert that any such fields solve an evolution
problem.

Use the time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, smooth future unit observer congruence, and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Here a **frame** means this smooth observer field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$ and its pointwise rest spaces; it does not mean a coordinate chart or a tetrad. On a nonempty open region $O$, take a $C^2$ fixed-composition state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, state function $e\in C^2(X)$, and $T=\partial_{\sigma_p}e>0$ as adopted by [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]]. The mathematical state maps are $n=v^{-1}$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\varepsilon=ne$, and $p=-\partial_v e$; their meanings and units are those in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]].

Write $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the rest-space projector, derivative along the observer congruence, expansion, acceleration, and spatial symmetric trace-free shear by
$$\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^a u^b,\qquad D=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta=\nabla_a u^a,\qquad a_b=u^c\nabla_c u_b,$$
$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$
where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Put $Y_b=\nabla_bT+Ta_b$ and $Z_b=\nabla_b(\mu/T)$, using the chemical potential $\mu$ from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. The number current, stress tensor and entropy current in the selected branch are
$$J^a=nu^a+V^a,\qquad \mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T},$$
with $u_aV^a=u_aQ^a=u_a\pi^{ab}=0$ and $\pi^{ab}$ symmetric and trace-free. Adopt the source-free balances $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0$ together with the first-order gradient closures
$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\qquad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\qquad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}Y_b,\qquad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}Z_b.$$

Here $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\theta$, $a_b$ and $\sigma_{ab}$ have inverse-length components; $\Pi$, $\pi^{ab}$ and $Q^a$ have units Pa; $\zeta,\eta\in C^1(O)$ have units Pa s; $\kappa\in C^1(O)$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$; and $L\in C^1(O)$ has formal units $\mathrm{marker^2\,K\,J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. The temperature and chemical-potential gradients have units K m$^{-1}$ and J marker$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ m$^{-1}$, respectively. The coefficient fields satisfy $\zeta,\eta,\kappa,L\geq0$. All displayed constitutive fields, currents and stress data are required to have enough regularity that the balances and entropy-current divergence hold classically.

Each application declares a nonempty open regime of the pointwise state values and first covariant derivatives of $u,T,\mu/T$ (with the listed algebraic constraints) on which the constitutive model is used. The regime separately requires $J$ to be future timelike. Since $u_aV^a=0$, this condition is $n>0$ and $g_{ab}V^aV^b<n^2$, as follows from $g(J,J)=-n^2+g(V,V)$ and $-u_aJ^a=n$. It is an additional applicability restriction, not a consequence of the gradient closures.

This is an adopted constitutive model for one declared material regime. The closures are not derived from geometry, measurements, or the second law; they do not assert that a solution exists, that the model applies to every material, or that the branch is causal, stable, or globally entropy-increasing. No empirical observation is supplied.

On an open region of the smooth spacetime of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], take a separately specified material/current model in its declared smooth regime. Its entropy current is a supplied $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ of the type and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Adopt the local admissibility condition

$$\nabla_aS^a\geq 0$$

throughout that region. This inequality is a physical restriction on the chosen model and current; it is not a construction of an undefined constitutive current. Each application must state its current, regime, boundary/exchange data, and any source or sink terms it includes.

The inequality is not deduced from Lorentzian geometry, the local state function, or finite data. It does not assert statistical thermalization, a universal microscopic $H$-theorem, entropy-area identification, or a generalized second law. Romatschke's cited calculation is restricted to a specified conformal-fluid model and itself records the absence of experimental verification known to that author; that source limitation does not turn this postulate into an observed law. No experimental observation or uncertainty is supplied by this item.

Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

derivations.claim:
The balances in [F2] are those of [F1] with $f^b=0$. By [F4], $\Delta$ is the orthogonal projector onto $u^\perp$; hence the closures make $Q$ and $V$ spatial. The defining projection in $\sigma$ makes it symmetric and spatial, and its trace is $\Delta^{cd}
abla_{(c}u_{d)}-(	heta/3)\Delta^{ab}\Delta_{ab}=	heta-(	heta/3)3=0$, since $u^cu^d
abla_cu_d=	frac12u^c
abla_c(g(u,u))=0$. Thus $\pi=-2\eta c\sigma$ is also symmetric, spatial, and trace-free. The state, observer, and regularity hypotheses of [F1] are supplied by [F2], [F4], and the given actual solution. Applying [F1] therefore gives
$$
abla_aS^a=- rac{\Pi	heta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T}- rac{Q^aY_a}{T^2}-V^aZ_a.$$.

Substitute the closures of [F2] term by term: $-\Pi\theta/T=\zeta c\theta^2/T$, $-\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}/T=2\eta c\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}/T$, $-Q^aY_a/T^2=\kappa\Delta^{ab}Y_aY_b/(cT^2)$, and $-V^aZ_a=L\Delta^{ab}Z_aZ_b$. This yields the displayed equality.

For a covector $W_a$, let $w^a=g^{ab}W_b$. Then $\Delta^{ab}W_aW_b=g_{ab}w^aw^b+(u^aW_a)^2=g(w,w)+g(w,u)^2=g(\Delta w,\Delta w)$ by the projection identity in [F6]. Since $\Delta w\in u^\perp$ and $g$ is positive definite there, this quadratic form is nonnegative. The finite-dimensional positive rest space has an orthonormal basis by Gram–Schmidt; as $\sigma_{ab}$ is symmetric and spatial, $\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}$ is the sum of the nine squared spatial components. Hence every term in step 2.1 is nonnegative by [F2] and $T,c>0$. By [F3] the selected branch meets the adopted criterion.

By [F2], $[\zeta]=[\eta]=\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $[\kappa]=\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, and $[L]=\mathrm{marker^2\,K\,J^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$; $[\theta]=[\sigma]=[a]=\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, $[Y]=\mathrm{K\,m^{-1}}$, and $[Z]=\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}\,K^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$. Each term in step 2.1 therefore has units J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-4}$; [F5] identifies $c\nabla_aS^a$ as the physical rate per volume in J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use the fixed-composition local-equilibrium state, smooth time-oriented Lorentzian geometry of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, smooth future unit observer congruence $u$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$ from [[post-tgr-local-material-thermodynamics]] and [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. In particular, $n>0$, $T>0$, $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, and $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$ have those suppliers' meanings. In a selected bulk-only branch, adopt the stress, number current, and source-free balances
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^a u^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$
where $\Pi$ is a smooth scalar bulk pressure. Let $\zeta,\tau\in C^1(O)$ be positive coefficient fields with SI units Pa s and s, respectively, and define $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, with units Pa$^{-1}$. Adopt the extended entropy current and derivative-corrected relaxation law
$$S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,\qquad \beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right).$$
Here $\Pi$ has units Pa, $D$ and $\theta$ have inverse-length units, and each side of the relaxation law has units m$^{-1}$; $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has entropy-density units J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$.

For each application, specify a nonempty open near-equilibrium regime in the pointwise state and first-derivative data around $\Pi=0$, based at constant zero-gradient reference data, and use the current and law only while the fields remain in that declared regime. Require enough field regularity for the balances and entropy divergence to hold classically. The mathematical result [[lem-tgr-bulk-relaxation-entropy]] supplies the exact matching conditional entropy identity and one homogeneous witness; its actual statement and proof are conditional on the listed mathematical inputs and assume exactly countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). It motivates this selection and is used by the downstream deductions, but it does not derive the adopted physical postulate.

This is a restricted constitutive assumption for the selected material. It does not derive the equation of state, assert universal validity, or adopt existence of a general nonlinear solution. It makes no causal or stability claim; positive relaxation time alone supplies neither. No empirical observation is supplied.

Use the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian data, local state, and conventions of [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]], with $n>0$, $T>0$, $c>0$, $x^0=ct$, and smooth future unit $u$. Assume positive $C^1$ coefficients $\zeta$ and $\tau$, set $\beta=\tau/\zeta$, and let $\Pi$ be a smooth scalar. In the bulk-only branch take

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad \nabla_aT^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ^a=0,$$

where $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_au^a$, and $a^b_{\rm acc}=Du^b$. Adopt the corrected relaxation law

$$\beta D\Pi+\frac{\Pi}{\zeta c}=-\theta-\frac{T\Pi}{2}\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\beta u^a}{T}\right)$$

and the extended entropy current $S^a=[s-\beta\Pi^2/(2T)]u^a$. Then the stress and particle equations imply

$$D\epsilon+(h+\Pi)\theta=0,\qquad (h+\Pi)a^b_{\rm acc}+\Delta^{ba}\nabla_a(p+\Pi)=0,\qquad Dn+n\theta=0,$$

and every actual smooth solution of the stated corrected law satisfies

$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\ge0.$$

Here $\beta$ has units $\mathrm{Pa^{-1}}$, $\Pi,\epsilon,p,h$ have units Pa, $D,\theta,a_{\rm acc}$ have inverse-length components, and the correction $\beta\Pi^2/(2T)$ has the units of entropy density. The law is an explicit model assumption; dropping its derivative term does not yield the stated sign identity in general.

There is an exact homogeneous solution on the explicitly specified Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$; its Levi-Civita derivative is ordinary coordinate differentiation. Fix a state point $(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ in the supplied local state domain with $v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_{p0})>0$, and take the constant state map $(v,\sigma_p)(x)=(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, so $n_0=1/v_0$, $\epsilon_0=n_0e(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$, and $p_0=-e_v(v_0,\sigma_{p0})$ are constant. For constant positive coefficients $\zeta_0,\tau_0$, let $u=\partial_{x^0}=(1,0,0,0)$, $T=T_0$, and define the smooth scalar field $\Pi(x)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0}$ on all of $M$, where $t=x^0/c$. The stress and particle balances and the corrected law hold, with strict entropy production wherever $\Pi(x)\ne0$. This mathematical witness is not a general nonlinear existence theorem or a claim of physical applicability in any separately selected near-equilibrium regime.

Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

The mathematical proof chain carries exactly [A1]. Applying [F2] yields $\nabla_aS^a=\Pi^2/(\zeta cT)$; since $\Pi^2\geq0$ and $\zeta,c,T>0$, this is nonnegative.

For the witness, the constant state gives constant $n_0,\varepsilon_0,p_0,T_0,s_0$. In the stated Minkowski coordinates, $u^0=1$, $u^i=0$, $\Delta^{00}=\Delta^{0i}=0$, and $\Delta^{ij}=\delta^{ij}$. Thus $J^0=n_0$, $J^i=0$, $\mathsf T^{00}=\varepsilon_0$, $\mathsf T^{0i}=0$, and $\mathsf T^{ij}=(p_0+\Pi(t))\delta^{ij}$. Since the only nonconstant component depends on time and occurs in spatial slots, $
abla_aJ^a=0$, $
abla_a\mathsf T^{a0}=\partial_{x^0}\varepsilon_0=0$, and $
abla_a\mathsf T^{ai}=\partial_{x^j}[(p_0+\Pi(t))\delta^{ji}]=0$ for $i=1,2,3$.

In SI length coordinates, $[\Pi]=\mathrm{Pa}$ and $[\zeta cT]=\mathrm{Pa\,s}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\,\mathrm K=\mathrm{Pa\,m\,K}$, so $[\Pi^2/(\zeta cT)]=\mathrm{Pa\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, in agreement with [F4]. Multiplication by $c$ gives J K$^{-1}$ m$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$.

Here $\theta=0$, $\nabla_a(\beta u^a/T_0)=0$, and $D\Pi=\partial_{x^0}\Pi=c^{-1}\partial_t\Pi=-\Pi/(c\tau_0)$. Therefore the left side of the corrected law is $-(\tau_0/\zeta_0)\Pi/(c\tau_0)+\Pi/(\zeta_0c)=0$, matching its right side. For fixed $\delta$, $|\Pi(t)|$ and $|D\Pi(t)|$ are bounded on $t> -\delta$ by $|\Pi_0|e^{\delta/\tau_0}$ and $|\Pi_0|e^{\delta/\tau_0}/(c\tau_0)$; taking $|\Pi_0|$ sufficiently small keeps all field and first-derivative data in the stated open regime.

Steps 1.2 and 2.2 verify that the specified fields are an actual smooth solution in the model regime. Applying the conditional identity from step 1.1 pointwise gives $\nabla_aS^a=\Pi(t)^2/(\zeta_0cT_0)=\Pi_0^2e^{-2t/\tau_0}/(\zeta_0cT_0)$. Its denominator is positive, hence production is zero for $\Pi_0=0$ and strictly positive for every finite $t\geq0$ when $\Pi_0\ne0$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

On a nonempty open region of the smooth $(-,+,+,+)$ Lorentzian model of [[post-tgr-bulk-relaxation-model]], assume an actual solution of its source-free stress and particle balances and corrected relaxation law. Use the state maps and units of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[def-tgr-framework-units]], with smooth future unit observer congruence $u$ (the frame, not a chart or tetrad), $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $n,T,c>0$, positive $C^1$ coefficient fields $\zeta,\tau$, and $\beta=\tau/\zeta$. Require enough regularity that all displayed balances and the entropy-current divergence are classical. The solution remains in the application's declared open near-equilibrium regime. With
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a,\qquad S^a=\left(s-\frac{\beta\Pi^2}{2T}\right)u^a,$$
the exact pointwise identity is
$$\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\Pi^2}{\zeta cT}\geq0.$$
This is conditional on an actual solution and does not assert general solution existence.

There is also an explicit homogeneous solution under the additional application condition that the declared open regime contains constant zero-gradient reference data with $\Pi=0$. Let the selected material's state domain contain $(v_0,\sigma_0)$ with $n_0=1/v_0>0$ and $T_0=e_{\sigma_p}(v_0,\sigma_0)>0$, and let the regime contain those constant state data. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2$, and future direction $\partial_{x^0}$, choose constant positive $\zeta_0,\tau_0$ and set $u=\partial_{x^0}$. For some $\delta>0$ seconds take the open region $O=(-c\delta,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3$, put $t=x^0/c$, and define
$$\Pi(t)=\Pi_0e^{-t/\tau_0},\qquad t> -\delta.$$
Choose $\Pi_0$ sufficiently small that the full field and first-derivative data stay in the declared regime throughout $O$. Then the source-free balances and corrected law hold, and the entropy production is strictly positive at every finite $t\geq0$ when $\Pi_0\ne0$, and zero when $\Pi_0=0$.

The argument is a conditional model deduction, not an observation or a general nonlinear existence, causality, or stability theorem. No empirical premise is used.

derivations.claim: In these global coordinates $g(u,u)=-1$ and $u=\partial_{x^0}$ is future-directed. The constant state makes $n_0,\varepsilon_0,p_0,T_0,s_0$ constant, while $\Pi$ depends only on $t=x^0/c$. The projector has $\Delta^{00}=\Delta^{0i}=0$ and $\Delta^{ij}=\delta^{ij}$.

Consequently $J^0=n_0$, $J^i=0$, $\mathsf T^{00}=\varepsilon_0$, $\mathsf T^{0i}=0$, and $\mathsf T^{ij}=(p_0+\Pi(t))\delta^{ij}$. The only nonconstant stress components have spatial indices and are spatially constant, so $
abla_aJ^a=0$, $
abla_a\mathsf T^{a0}=\partial_{x^0}\varepsilon_0=0$, and $
abla_a\mathsf T^{ai}=\partial_{x^j}[(p_0+\Pi(t))\delta^{ji}]=0$ for each $i=1,2,3$.

The constant $u,T_0,\beta=\tau_0/\zeta_0$ give $\theta=0$ and $\nabla_a(\beta u^a/T_0)=0$. Also $D\Pi=c^{-1}\partial_t\Pi=-\Pi/(c\tau_0)$, so $\beta D\Pi+\Pi/(\zeta_0c)=-(\tau_0/\zeta_0)\Pi/(c\tau_0)+\Pi/(\zeta_0c)=0$, equal to the right side of the corrected law. By the amplitude choice in [given], the whole solution lies in the declared open regime.

Steps 1.1, 2.1, and 2.2 verify an actual smooth solution of every hypothesis in [F1], including the model regime.
